ds: Use of casinos, online gaming and betting to convert illicit cash into seemingly legitimate winnings or cheques, to move value between parties, or to obscure its origin through chips, accounts and junkets. Minimal play with high buy-ins is a classic sign.

src.t: FATF, Vulnerabilities of Casinos and Gaming Sector (2009)
FATF, Guidance on the Risk-Based Approach for Casinos (2008)
FATF, Risks of Gaming and Gambling (Red Flag Risk Indicators) (2026-09-09)

cn.rt: Consumers fund gambling and cash out winnings via Everyday account payments and card spend; casino-floor chips and junkets are out of scope.

rat: Casino chip purchase/cash-out, deposit accounts, junkets; funded by cash and bank sources.

ind.n: Large cash buy-in with minimal gambling
ind.cx: Customer buys chips with cash, plays little, and cashes out.
ind.ds: Substantial funds are deposited or bought in with minimal gambling or betting activity before withdrawal.
ind.cn: Large buy-in or deposits with little underlying activity

ind.n: Chips passed between players or taken away
ind.cx: Chips transferred between customers or cashed by third parties.
ind.ds: Chips transferred between customers or cashed by third parties.

ind.n: Funds deposited and withdrawn from casino account with little play
ind.cx: Casino deposit accounts used like bank accounts.
ind.ds: Casino deposit accounts used like bank accounts.

ind.n: Use of multiple identities or accounts
ind.cx: Same person plays under different names or accounts.
ind.ds: The same individual appears under different names or opens several accounts or wallets, directly or through an intermediary.
ind.cn: One person holding multiple identities or accounts

ind.cx: Funds from third parties or unusual bank sources pay for play.
ind.ds: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
ind.cn: Payments from or to unrelated third parties

ind.n: Junket or VIP operators moving funds across borders
ind.cx: Junket arrangements shift large funds without clear play.
ind.ds: Junket arrangements shift large funds without clear play.

ind.n: Online gaming accounts with deposit via multiple cards or wallets
ind.cx: Multiple payment instruments for an account with low play.
ind.ds: Multiple payment instruments for an account with low play.

ind.cx: Requests for win certificates or cheques not matching records.
ind.ds: Requests for win certificates or cheques not matching records.

ind.cx: Players lose deliberately to a counterpart.
ind.ds: Players lose deliberately to a counterpart.

ind.n: Gambling account holder does not match the payment method used to fund or withdraw
ind.cx: Online betting or casino account details differ from the owner of the funding or withdrawal payment method.
ind.fp: Joint accounts or family cards used with consent and disclosed.
ind.ds: Details on an online betting or casino account differ from the owner of the card, bank account or wallet used for deposits and withdrawals.

ind.n: Gambler conceals identity or location with repeated VPN use, many devices or mismatched residence
ind.cx: Players conceal identity or location using VPNs, multiple devices or mismatched residence.
ind.fp: Privacy-conscious users, travellers or corporate VPNs.
ind.ds: A player repeatedly uses VPNs or multiple devices, or their detected location conflicts with their declared residence.

ctl.ds: Surveils chip transfers, buy-in versus play, low-risk or hedged betting, unusual stakes and collusive play between accounts or players. It detects use of gaming or betting products to launder or manipulate outcomes.

Restricts cash-out and cheque issue to evidenced winnings, prohibits redemption to third parties and issues win certificates only on verified records, with periodic audit. It prevents gaming proceeds being used as a conduit for illicit funds.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.
